પોતાના ઉદ્દેશો બર લાવવા,વહીવટી સાનુફુળતા: To fulfil its objectives and for administrative convenience, in 1961-62 the Bank purchased a plot with some buildings from the District Committee for Rs. 31,551/- so that a modern head office could be built at Himmatnagar. The Bank then began constructing its own building, with provision for a safe deposit vault / lockers, on a war footing. Within less than six years of starting work, the Bank got its own building, and the entrance of the Bank's modern building shone on the cover of the eighth annual report. Today, 29 of the Bank's 115 branches have their own buildings.
બેંકના ઉદભવ પહેલાં અર્થાત સને ૧૯૬૦ પહેલા: Before the Bank came into being, that is before 1960, The Bombay State Co-op. Bank Ltd. worked as the central financing agency in this district. In 1949 it opened its first branch at Himmatnagar, followed by branches at Talod in 1950, Modasa in 1951, Idar in 1958 and Khedbrahma in 1959. However, the control of funds needed by the farmers of Sabarkantha for agriculture rested in Mumbai, which was inconvenient in many ways. As per the procedure laid down by the Reserve Bank of India for starting a District Central Cooperative Bank in every district, The Sabarkantha District Central Cooperative Bank Ltd. was registered and established as stated earlier, and began operations on the first day of January 1960, the first day of the new year. It should be noted that at the time of the Bank's establishment, i.e. up to 1959, Sabarkantha had only four branches of two (nationalised) banks: Punjab National Bank, started at Himmatnagar in 1951, State Bank of India, started in 1956, and State Bank of India branches started at Modasa and Idar in 1957. This picture clearly shows the necessity of a District Central Cooperative Bank for the all-round development of the district. With the birth of the Sabarkantha Bank on 15/4/1959, the people of the district felt a joy like "Nand Gher Anand Bhayo". The faith of the sentimental people of this land bore fruit and a new work began. True faith always gives bright results, as Gani Dahiwala has said, has he not?

The Bank's main objective is to ensure that the district's farmers receive agricultural and non-agricultural credit, that their agricultural produce increases progressively, and that this district thereby achieves unparalleled prosperity.

સાબરકાંઠા અને અરવલ્લી જીલ્લાના ગ્રાહકો,: I feel joy in warmly welcoming you all on the occasion of the launch of the website of our Sabarkantha Bank, which has been climbing the steps of continuous growth since 1959 through the co-operative movement that touches, directly or indirectly, the customers, villages and every household of the Sabarkantha and Aravalli districts. Sensing the pulse of the times and with the aim of making the maximum use of modern technology, the Bank has brought all its branches onto the Core Banking Solution (CBS) platform and has begun offering its customers facilities on par with other banks.
સાબરકાંઠાની વસ્તીના રર ટકા ઉપરાંતની વસ્ત: With more than 22 percent of Sabarkantha's population belonging to backward classes including tribals, and given the inadequate spread of education, it was essential that the co-operative movement started at that time be given proper momentum with the aim of the welfare of the many. With the aim that the people of Sabarkantha could develop economically and that the various co-operative units set up for that purpose would face no financial difficulty, The Sabarkantha District Central Cooperative Bank Ltd. was registered on the auspicious day of the fifteenth of April 1959 under registration no. 24935, and its official existence was announced.
હિંમતનગર ખાતે હાજીપુર વિસ્તારમાં ભાડાના: The Bank's head office began work on 1/1/1960 in a rented building in the Hajipur area of Himmatnagar. Before that, five branches of The Bombay State Co-operative Bank Ltd. were working in this district; the Sabarkantha Bank took over their administration and began its activities in its own style. In the year of the Bank's establishment there were only 49 staff in these five branches, which has grown today to 699 in 115 branches. While taking charge of the five branches, within a very short time, on 13/7/1960, the Bhiloda branch started work, and thereafter expansion continued in all directions of this district.
